items.title: Retail Crowd Dump Vietnam Stocks for Near 10% Bank-Deposit Rates
points: (Bloomberg) -- Vietnam’s retail investors are dumping equities and buying high-yielding notes from banks to capture interest rates nearing 10%, as locals and foreigners fall out of favor with the poor-performing stock market.
Banks lifted deposit rates in recent months to compete for funding, sucking in a swathe of the country’s 14 million retail investors to a financial product long considered out of fashion.
The move came as the roughly $392 billion equity market dropped about 3% in 2026, on course for its first annual loss in four years.

Still, persistent selling of equities by oversees money managers and local individual investors preferring the safety of high returning bank notes has left the benchmark stock index about 24% below its price-earnings multiple of the past five years.

Cash held in Vietnamese investors’ securities accounts dropped to about 64.9 trillion dong ($2.5 billion) at the end of the third quarter, down 49% from a year earlier and the lowest level since the fourth quarter of 2024, according to data compiled by…

items.title: Emerging-Market Assets Dip as Chip Rout, Fed Rate Worries Linger
points: (Bloomberg) -- Emerging-market assets fell on Friday as a rout in chipmakers weighed on equities and lingering concerns over the Federal Reserve’s rate path kept currencies under pressure.
An index for emerging-market currencies fell less than 0.1% after an end-of-day adjustment, and most currencies weakened against the dollar.

US producer prices climbed in October from a year earlier at the fastest pace since 2022, but the data came slightly below estimates, capping a week dominated by surging bets on Federal Reserve rate hikes, as well as Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia Corp.

“The PPI number took some pressure off the Fed to hike by 50 basis points, but EM investors are still nervous about the final destination for the Fed, as we are looking at higher rates for longer,” said Paresh Upadhyaya, a strategist at Pioneer Investments.
MSCI’s gauge for emerging-market stocks fell on Friday, but was still up more than 3% this week, with South Korea and Taiwan’s AI-dominated stock gauges gaining.

items.title: Australia Bauxite: Fewer Cargoes Overall, but More of Them Bound for China

China’s share of Australia’s total bauxite exports rose to 70.8%, up from 65.6% a year earlier.
The divergence was more pronounced in October, when China-bound shipments increased 13.6% year-over-year to 4.37 Mt, while volumes to other destinations fell 23.9%.

items.title: Iron Ore Port Inventory and Port Pick-up Volume on November 13, 2026
points: As of November 13, SMM’s latest statistics show that total iron ore inventory across 35 main ports nationwide reached 152.12 million mt, up 2.99 million mt MoM, with overall inventory on an accumulation trend.
Daily average port pick-up volume edged down 40,000 mt to 3.08 million mt.
Iron ore port inventory has recently been on an uptrend.
On the supply side, port arrivals rose sharply as resources arrived in concentrated waves.

On the demand side, hot metal production pulled back due to environmental protection-driven production restrictions and other factors, while steel mill purchasing and cargo pick-up pace slowed, dragging overall port pick-up volume lower.
With arrivals increasing and port pick-up declining, port inventory continued to accumulate.
Looking ahead to next week, port arrivals are expected to pull back, but port pick-up volume is likely to extend its decline.

items.title: Conab lifts Brazil 2026-27 soybean oil export forecast to 1.8 mil mt

points: A 13-year-old boy died of electrocution after coming into contact with a snapped stay wire attached to an electric pole in a paddy field in Malappuram on Sunday (November 15).
The deceased, identified as Junaid, son of Shihabudheen of Cherumukku in Tirurangadi, had gone to the field with friends to watch a tractor plough the land, the police said.
Residents said Junaid’s friends tried to rescue him, but the tractor driver stopped them from approaching the wire, saving them from a similar fate.

items.title: US extends Jones Act waiver into February
points: Washington has extended its Jones Act waiver for another 90 days, allowing foreign-flagged vessels to continue competing for selected domestic cargo movements between US ports into February next year.
The Department of Homeland Security approved the third extension of the waiver introduced in March, according to a November 13 notice from US Customs and Border Protection.
Eligible cargo must be loaded before 11.59 pm Eastern Time on February 14, 2027.
Foreign-flagged ships will still need individual approval before undertaking coastwise voyages.

Cargo interests must submit vessel availability requests to the relevant US authorities, after which the Maritime Administration will survey the market to determine whether suitable Jones Act-qualified tonnage is available.
The requirement keeps the tighter approval system introduced in August rather than restoring the broader exemptions available earlier in the year.
The waiver was initially introduced in March amid disruption to US fuel supplies and shipping markets following the outbreak of war with Iran.

points: Guest teachers in Haryana schools held a mock Assembly at the Mini Secretariat in Kurukshetra on Saturday, demanding regularisation under the three-year policy notified in 2014 in accordance with court orders.

items.title: India eases flag rules in push for more tonnage
points: India has relaxed its ship registration rules, allowing vessels with majority Indian ownership to qualify for the national flag in a move that opens the door to foreign minority investment.

The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways has set the ownership threshold at more than 50%, replacing the full qualifying Indian ownership requirement imposed under the previous Merchant Shipping Act.
A government notification published in the Gazette of India sets out the new conditions under the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025.
Qualifying owners include Indian citizens, non-resident Indians, overseas citizens of India, Indian-incorporated companies, cooperatives and limited liability partnerships.
The change does not automatically give qualifying ships the right to fly the Indian flag.
The move comes during a wider push by New Delhi to increase Indian-flagged tonnage and strengthen its domestic shipping industry.

Splash reported last year that MSC, Maersk and CMA CGM were looking to shift vessels onto the Indian register, while Hapag-Lloyd signed agreements with the government in March covering possible reflagging of up to four ships.

points: Mumbai recently held an online event to honor the birth centenary of Nobel laureate Abdus Salam.
Eminent scientist Pervez Amirali Hoodbhoy delivered a lecture discussing Salam's contributions to physics and his life.
Hoodbhoy highlighted Salam's significance as a symbol of goodwill between India and Pakistan.
He mentioned Salam's lack of recognition in Pakistan due to his Ahmadiyya sect affiliation, affecting youth role models.

items.title: Kashmir film fraternity trains guns on Bollywood’s ‘AK-47 & skullcap’ stereotype, seeks own industry
points: Kashmiri filmmakers are advocating for a shift towards regional cinema to enhance authentic storytelling and representation.
They argue that Bollywood often reinforces stereotypes that misrepresent life in J&K.
The current film policy is criticized for not adequately supporting local productions while favoring external filmmakers.
Actors and directors are calling for collaboration among regional artists to develop a unique Kashmiri film industry, signaling a significant movement towards self-identity and cultural expression.

items.title: 'Well-planned conspiracy': BJP refutes reports of 209-candidate list for upcoming UP elections
points: The Bharatiya Janata Party's Uttar Pradesh unit has refuted claims regarding a supposed list of 209 candidates.
Officials described these reports as false and part of a larger scheme.
They cautioned party members against believing in unverified media stories.
Additionally, they clarified that the assembly election candidate selection process has yet to commence, highlighting the importance of a methodical and unified approach to such decisions.

items.title: 'Divide-and-rule tactics': RSS chief Bhagwat's warning over attempts to split India
points: During a recent event in Jodhpur, RSS leader Mohan Bhagwat spoke fervently about the necessity of national unity.
He indicated that smaller identities can lead to societal rifts, reminiscent of colonial tactics.
Emphasizing the need for individuals to set aside ego and self-interest, he illustrated his points with lessons from the Mahabharata, stressing that unity is key to overcoming challenges.
